title: Underlying lifting-fibre comparison for etale inverse image
statement: For a morphism f:Y→X [def-pc-scheme], a short exact sequence S of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and a global section s of its quotient, set inverse image [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] of the canonical lifting torsor [lem-sc-torsor-h1] is isomorphic to the canonical lifting torsor of the pulled-back section. On sections in the image of the set adjunction unit, its inclusion into the pulled-back middle sheaf equals the abelian adjunction unit applied to the original lift.

source.place: Tags 00X6 and 03AJ; the equalizer-of-a-section argument of parent step 2

proof.text: Construct the quotient map and the constant restriction-of-s map on the underlying middle sheaf. The subtype inclusion is a limiting fork, with lifts and uniqueness proved sectionwise.

Use finite-limit preservation and the natural underlying-abelian comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures]. Deduce compatibility of its inverse with units from the hom-set equation at the identity and the identity-on-sections direct-image comparison. Unfold global-section pullback and use terminal uniqueness and unit naturality to identify the restriction of the pulled-back section. The adjunction hom-set bijection is injective, so these equations identify the two constant-section maps after inverse image.

Map the limiting fork using isLimitForkMapOfIsLimit. Transport its diagram by the comparison isomorphisms via Fork.equivOfIsos and Fork.isLimitOfIsos. Compose with the target subtype limiting fork using conePointUniqueUpToIso. Evaluate conePointUniqueUpToIso_hom_comp, then use unit naturality for the subtype inclusion and the unit comparison to obtain the asserted equation.

proof_origin.note: Complete Lean equalizer proof specialized from parent step 2; no remaining hole.
